tagline: Between Baxter's two gates, with Katahdin keeping watch.
intro: From the south gate of Baxter State Park the byway passes between Ambajejus and Millinocket lakes into Millinocket, then runs by East Millinocket and Medway and up Route 11 beside the Penobscot through Stacyville to Patten, and on to Baxter's north gate at Grand Lake Matagamon, 89 miles in all. Katahdin, 5,268 feet and the northern end of the Appalachian Trail, dominates the country. On the way, Grindstone Falls spreads some 300 feet wide.

Thoreau came through in 1846 with Millinocket's Fowler family as guides and wrote it up in The Maine Woods. Governor Percival Baxter later bought more than 200,000 acres, Katahdin included, with his own money and gave them to the people of Maine, to stay forever wild.

moments.title: Millinocket
moments.text: Great Northern Paper had to build a town around its new mill, and the Magic City drew spectators from all over to watch it rise out of the wilderness.

moments.title: Ash Hill
moments.text: Just south of Patten the hill looks all the way around, to Katahdin and the Baxter mountains and far off toward the Allagash and Aroostook County.

moments.title: Patten
moments.text: The Lumbermen's Museum fills nine buildings with the woodsman's tools from the 1800s into the 1920s, with room for the river drivers, their bateaux and the bean hole beans.
